title: NORVASC (amlodipine besylate) tablets for oral administration: full prescribing information
authors: US Food and Drug Administration (labelling submitted by Viatris Specialty LLC)
journal: US Food and Drug Administration-approved labelling, published in DailyMed (National Library of Medicine); structured product label version 10, published 10 December 2025, label text revised 2/2023
funder: not stated; FDA-approved labelling carries no funding statement
result: Initial US approval 1992. Contraindication: known sensitivity to amlodipine only; the label carries no boxed warning. Warnings and precautions: symptomatic hypotension is possible, particularly with severe aortic stenosis, although acute hypotension is unlikely because of the gradual onset; worsening angina and acute myocardial infarction can develop after starting or increasing the dose, particularly with severe obstructive coronary artery disease; titrate slowly in severe hepatic impairment, because the plasma elimination half-life is 56 hours in patients with impaired hepatic function. Placebo-controlled trials (amlodipine n=1730, placebo n=1250): discontinuation for adverse reactions about 1.5% against about 1%; dose-related oedema 1.8% (2.5 mg, n=275), 3.0% (5 mg, n=296) and 10.8% (10 mg, n=268) against 0.6% (placebo, n=520); palpitation 0.7%, 1.4% and 4.5% against 0.6%; flushing 0.7%, 1.4% and 2.6% against 0.0%; oedema 14.6% of 512 women and 5.6% of 1218 men against 5.1% and 1.4% on placebo. Events in fewer than 1% but more than 0.1% of patients in controlled or open trials or marketing experience, causal relationship uncertain, include arrhythmia (including ventricular tachycardia and atrial fibrillation), bradycardia, syncope, vasculitis, peripheral neuropathy, tremor, constipation, dysphagia, pancreatitis, gingival hyperplasia, angioedema, erythema multiforme, depression, sexual dysfunction, nocturia, micturition frequency, hyperglycaemia, leukopenia, purpura and thrombocytopenia. Postmarketing: gynaecomastia; jaundice and hepatic enzyme elevations, mostly consistent with cholestasis or hepatitis, in some cases severe enough to require hospitalisation; a possible association with extrapyramidal disorder. Interactions: moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increase amlodipine exposure (diltiazem 180 mg raised it by 60% in elderly patients; erythromycin did not change it significantly in healthy volunteers; itraconazole and clarithromycin may raise it further); monitor for hypotension and oedema; no quantitative information on CYP3A inducers; monitor for hypotension with sildenafil; amlodipine is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, raised simvastatin exposure by 77% at 80 mg so simvastatin is limited to 20 mg daily, raised trough ciclosporin by an average 40% in 11 renal transplant patients and tacrolimus exposure 2.5-fold to 4-fold in 9 CYP3A5 expressers, with a 3-fold rise reported in one CYP3A5 non-expresser; cimetidine, antacids, sildenafil and grapefruit juice had no impact on amlodipine exposure. Pharmacodynamics: negative inotropic effects can be detected in vitro but have not been seen in intact animals at therapeutic doses; no change in sinoatrial nodal function or atrioventricular conduction in intact animals or man; serum calcium is not affected. Clinical studies of NORVASC did not include sufficient numbers of patients aged 65 or over to determine whether they respond differently; clearance falls in elderly patients, raising AUC by about 40 to 60%. Overdose may cause excessive peripheral vasodilation with marked hypotension and possibly reflex tachycardia; human experience with intentional overdose is limited; haemodialysis is not likely to help because the drug is highly protein bound. Pregnancy: post-marketing data insufficient to inform drug-associated risk; in rats a dose about 10 times the maximum human dose halved litter size, raised intrauterine deaths about 5-fold and prolonged gestation and labour. Lactation: median relative infant dose 4.2%. Heart failure: in a placebo-controlled study of 1153 patients with NYHA class III or IV heart failure (mean 13.8 months) the combined end point occurred in 222 of 571 (39%) on amlodipine and 246 of 583 (42%) on placebo; in PRAISE-2 (827 against 827 patients with non-ischaemic NYHA III or IV heart failure, mean 33 months) all-cause mortality did not differ (95% confidence limits from an 8% reduction to a 29% increase) and there were more reports of pulmonary oedema with amlodipine.
